A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, references, and Appendices A–D support comparison, including the revised proofs and additional experiment in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original decentralized-training experiments, including communication-window comparisons, final-merging results, loss landscapes, and sensitivity analyses in Figures 1–2 and C.1–C.5.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds results for topology-constrained final gossip merging in Figure C.6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, sparse peer communication, and final parameter averaging remain unchanged. V2 already describes approximating global merging through multiple gossip rounds in Section 4.2; v3 evaluates specific instances of that existing option in Appendix C.3.4.

E1.justification: The image-classification datasets and task coverage are retained. Figure C.6 uses the existing Tiny ImageNet task and exponential graph family; its addition concerns the final aggregation procedure rather than a new dataset, population, or prediction task.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same federated, decentralized, and local or one-shot training comparators. SCSP is newly discussed in Section 4.2, but no reported experiment evaluates it. Figure C.6 compares aggregation variants using the existing comparator families.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3.4 adds protocols using one or five final gossip rounds on an exponential graph, alongside random-topology training followed by a perfect global merge. Previously reported data partitions, training budgets, optimizers, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure C.6 adds a focused feasibility and sensitivity analysis of replacing exact final global aggregation with topology-constrained gossip, including the effect of one versus five rounds. Existing topology, initialization, hyperparameter, and heterogeneity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. Figure C.6 follows the existing practice of presenting accuracy curves without additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure C.6 adds results showing substantial accuracy recovery after final gossip merging, described as comparable to the perfect-global-merge reference. These are results under added evaluation protocols. The plotted results in Figures 1–2 and C.1–C.5 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D replace the positive-part, square-root A(t) convergence bound with a U(t)-based analysis and substantially revise learning-rate conditions and Propositions 2–3. V3 also revises smoothness assumptions, variance and Taylor coefficients, and consensus-bound constants; adds Proposition D.9's critical-consensus-edge proof; and discusses network-size scaling in Remark D.2. Section 4.2 revises the communication-cost calculation to linear-in-agent Ring-AllReduce costs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the headline claims that late communication and a single final merge improve global performance, limited nonzero communication preserves mergeability, and the merged DSGD model can match parallel SGD's convergence rate. The emphasized cross-initialization and cross-distribution setting was already described in v2's appendices.

C2.justification: V3 substantially revises the theoretical mechanism and its qualifications: Section 5.2 interprets progressive sharpening as potential acceleration beyond parallel SGD under a specific large-learning-rate regime, while Remark D.2 discusses increasing agent count as target accuracy tightens. Remark 2 additionally argues against cumulative gossip alone explaining the final performance jump. These alter the explanation and applicability of the central theoretical contribution.

D1.justification: V2 promises a future code release; v3 supplies concrete code-access links in the abstract and Section 4.1. Existing hardware, runtime, memory, preprocessing, and hyperparameter disclosures in Appendix C.1 are retained. The PDFs establish the changed access information, without verifying repository contents.

R1.justification: V3 adds Aketi et al. (2021) and distinguishes its work from SCSP through sparsification type and local-step settings. It also adds Polyak (1987) to position the large-learning-rate interpretation. The broader related-work framework remains intact; duplicate Kong et al. entries are consolidated.

P1.justification: V3 polishes and condenses passages in the abstract, introduction, related work, Q&A, and discussion, and replaces much empirical 'global generalization' wording with 'global test performance.' Remarks and proof exposition are reorganized, while the overall section and appendix structure is preserved.

P2.justification: V3 adds the three-panel Figure C.6, shortens Figure 1's caption, relocates Table 1, and adjusts surrounding layout. Existing empirical figures retain their plots and visual designs; there is no broad graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful gossip-merging evidence and code-access information and repairs several variance and Taylor coefficients. However, the central theoretical rewrite has unresolved inconsistencies: Theorem 1 omits the 1/epsilon factor on the cumulative U(t) term present in Table 1 and the proof, and Corollary D.4 changes a sign incompatibly with its defined expected increment. These problems affect the main theoretical contribution, leaving the net quality effect uncertain despite the empirical and documentation gains.
